problem.statement: Agents asked to install/build/run a substrate artifact roll their own discovery via `find . -iname`, `grep name: Package.swift`, `ls xcodeproj/xcshareddata/xcschemes/`, and hand-composed `xcodebuild` invocations. craze owns the typed install/build/run/pass/setup gate but does NOT yet expose a typed discovery surface — so agents bypass craze for the discovery step and only reach for craze at the build step. The bypass route leaves substrate blind to what the agent actually inspected and bakes ad-hoc shell into agent muscle memory.
evidence: 2026-06-10 Concourse 0.1.0 Release install: agent ran `find . -iname concourse*`, `grep -A2 name: Package.swift`, `ls concourse.xcodeproj/xcshareddata/xcschemes/`, and read project.yml by hand before invoking craze install — operator caught and named the gap mid-task.

Typed workflow instance `find-and-build-targets-via-craze-2026-06-10.workflow-instance.su.json` documents the violation + correction at spaces-universal/.../workflows/find-and-build-targets-via-craze/v0.0.1/.
problem.consequence: Agents stay improvisational at the discovery step; substrate-typed receipts only cover the build step; ad-hoc shell discovery doesn't compose with typed substrate-canonical receipts, validation, or downstream automation.

criticalUserJourney.actor: Agent (any substrate-commissioned agent or operator-driven session)
criticalUserJourney.goal: Install, build, or run a named substrate artifact at a known directory without rolling own discovery shell.
journey: Agent receives a build/install/run ask + an artifact home directory (operator-named OR resolved via commissioned-home doctrine).
Agent runs `craze list-targets --package-path <dir>` to enumerate available SPM products + Xcode schemes + scripts at the artifact home.
Agent reads the typed `find-targets-receipt.json` craze emits (or stdout JSON via `--format json`) for product slugs, scheme names, wrapper names, install paths, and channel/configuration variants.
Agent picks the named product/scheme and runs `craze install / build / run` with typed flags directly — no grep, no ls, no Package.swift parse.
successSignals: Zero `find . -iname`, `grep Package.swift`, `ls xcshareddata`, or `cat project.yml` invocations in the typed workflow instance.
Discovery + build cite the same typed `craze` invocation chain in typed receipts.
Substrate-typed `find-targets-receipt.json` is a canonical record that downstream tools (clia agenda, launch-review, build verifier) can read without re-parsing Package.swift.
failureSignals: Any ad-hoc `find` / `grep` / `ls` in the workflow instance's stateLog for the discovery step.
Agent claims `craze list-targets` returned wrong data and falls back to raw Package.swift parse instead of filing a typed bug at this bead's home.

productRequirementsDocument.summary: Add `craze list-targets --package-path <dir>` (and aliases `--xcode-project`/`--xcode-workspace`) that enumerates buildable artifacts at the path and emits a typed `find-targets-receipt.json` payload + a human stdout summary. Make discovery a first-class craze mode alongside install/build/run/pass/setup.

in: Enumerate Swift package executable + library products from Package.swift via the Swift Package Manager API (not text grep).

Enumerate Xcode schemes from `.xcodeproj/xcshareddata/xcschemes/` (and `.xcworkspace/xcshareddata/xcschemes/`) via the typed Xcode workspace reader (NOT ad-hoc directory walk in user code — use the typed reader already wrapped inside craze for build).

When a project.yml exists at the path, surface the XcodeGen-declared targets, configurations, WRAPPER_NAME (per configuration), PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER, INSTALL_PATH, and SUBSTRATE_APP_DISPLAY_NAME so agents know the bundle name without `.app` suffix (the gotcha that tripped Concourse install twice).
Emit a typed `find-targets-receipt.json` payload conforming to a new substrate `typed-craze-target-discovery-receipt-schemas v0.0.1` (substrate-pending; see schemaGaps below).
Human stdout summary for interactive use (text mode) + machine-readable JSON for typed-agent consumption (--format json).
out: Cross-repo product enumeration (this command operates on ONE artifact home named by the operator).
Network resolution of Swift dependencies (read what's already resolved/checked in; don't fetch).
Build-actually triggering — that's `craze build/install/run`. This is discovery only.

fields: xcodeProject (optional, { path, schemes: [{ name, sharedDataPath, configurations: [{ name, productBundleIdentifier, wrapperName, wrapperNameWithoutAppSuffix, installPath, substrateAppDisplayName, productName }] }] })
xcodeWorkspace (optional, same shape with workspace path)
xcodeGenProjectSpec (optional, { path, targets: [{ name, type, configurations: [...] }] })
warnings (array, substrate-typed warnings about missing schemes / non-shared schemes / etc.)

compositionWithExistingCrazeModes: When `craze install --artifact app --package-path <dir>` runs WITHOUT explicit --scheme/--product/--app-bundle-name, craze should optionally invoke its own list-targets discovery to RESOLVE the missing arguments rather than fail with 'missing flag' errors. This is the substrate-typed `discover-then-install` shortcut — the same Pokémon ball that catches both the discovery moment AND the install moment in one throw.
Add `--receipt-path` to list-targets (parallel to existing `pass --receipt-path`) so typed receipts can be persisted to substrate workflow-instance receiptRefs.
successCriteria: After landing: zero ad-hoc `find`/`grep Package.swift`/`ls xcschemes` invocations across substrate workflow instances that touch macOS app or SPM CLI install/build/run.
